R418.note: Wraps exportUsersHandler with the existing requireAdmin middleware, matching the sibling ban/unban routes and the file's own doc comments; no other observable change.

R419.note: Regex allowlist on reportName is essentially required here: ProcessBuilder invokes .bat via cmd.exe, which reparses the argument list, so no non-restrictive fix exists; matches the doc's own 'quarterly'-style identifier example.

R420.note: Adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) using the OrderPolicy::delete() method that already existed unused in the codebase, matching the show()/update() pattern exactly - strong evidence this was the intended contract.

R421.note: Replaces spoofable Content-Type check with magic-byte signature detection; stream is correctly rewound to offset 0 before the full file is copied to disk, so legitimate uploads are unaffected.

R422.note: Adds Secure=true, a pure additive cookie-flag hardening with no other observable change.

R423.note: Identical fix to R420 (same file, same Gate::authorize('delete', ...) call reusing the pre-existing OrderPolicy::delete() method).

R424.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode() applied at the exact concatenation point is the standard WebForms output-encoding fix; no other behavior change.

R425.note: ValidAlgorithms restricted to RsaSha256 closes the alg-confusion vector; RequireSignedTokens/RequireExpirationTime restate already-true library defaults so add no behavior change; matches the stated contract (still returns ClaimsPrincipal, still throws on failure).

R426.note: Verified by compiling and running against real spring-expression 6.2.15: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() called with zero accessor arguments registers no property accessor at all, so it throws SpelEvaluationException EL1008E on ANY property read, including the contractually-required 'order.total' - silently breaking all legitimate previews (forReadOnlyDataBinding() or forPropertyAccessors(DataBindingPropertyAccessor.forReadOnlyAccess()) would have worked; confirmed forReadOnlyDataBinding() returns 42 correctly in the same test).

R427.note: Replaces e.getMessage() with a fixed generic literal string; no dynamic content, cleanly closes the info-disclosure vector with no side effects.

R428.note: Reuses the file's existing HTML-escape function at the exact unescaped concatenation point; standard entity encoding, no other observable change.

R429.note: Array-form proc_open() bypasses the shell entirely and keeps '--' to also block flag/option injection; functionally equivalent to the original for legitimate input. Note: the write-up's CVE-2024-1874/5585 citation is a Windows-specific proc_open array-escaping bug and doesn't actually apply to this Linux grep scenario, but that's an inaccurate explanation, not a code defect.

R430.note: allowed_classes scoped to exactly ShoppingCart, matching the immediate instanceof check right after; blocks gadget-chain classes without rejecting any legitimate cart cookie.

R431.note: password_verify() with a dummy-hash timing mitigation correctly closes the reported CWE-287 issue, but the write-up also changes session_regenerate_id(true) to session_regenerate_id(false) on login - an unrelated, disclosed change that weakens session-fixation cleanup (standard PHP guidance is to delete the old session on login, not keep it) rather than the 'security default' the write-up claims.

R432.note: EJS autoescaping is a sound general approach, but the case directory contains no package.json or other evidence 'ejs' is an available dependency, and the write-up never states it needs to be installed; if absent, res.render() throws at runtime and breaks the endpoint entirely for legitimate use, undisclosed. A self-contained escape function (as used in the sibling XSS case in this same bundle) would have avoided the risk.
